I liked Overwatch a lot, and I'm an avid Spy main in TF2. A lot of the same skillsets cross over, but there are some fundamental differences between the two. Here's my thoughts for those that care:

TF2 differences:

  • low penalties for death encourages solo play
  • custom loadouts make the classes more versatile in roles (combat engineer, or demoknight)
  • more gamemodes
  • content updates are rare nowadays (tough break ended in march and theres been nothing since..)
  • cosmetics and taunts in tf2 allow players to feel "unique" compared to everyone else.
  • no real progression system (weapon drops are randomly timed and dont require actual playing i.e. idle servers)
  • valve servers only play the same few levels, need to specifically search a server for a level you enjoy if its not in rotation
  • free to play
  • spawncamping is much easier. Generally spawn rooms in tf2 are poorly done.
  • levels are all the same flavor. Desert and dust, with a few exceptions (borneo, suijin)

Overwatch differences:

  • 6v6 means death matters. A badly timed ult or death significantly impacts the team.
  • 21 characters means highly likely players will have one they enjoy (compared to 9)
  • not free to play means that players are less likely to see completely baffling new players doing the weirdest things (post launch obv)
  • team play encouraged. Queuing up with people rewards bonus experience
  • lootbox progression system is very solid, leveling feels good.
  • very few customization options for heros. Harder to feel "unique" like in an mmo or tf2.
  • character voice commands are really lacking. No "yes" "no" "go left" etc.
  • overall lack of character dialogue and banter makes heros feel less real.
  • sprays are pretty cool, need more unique and cool ones though
  • level design is top notch. Very beautiful
  • spawn rooms heal extremely fast making spawn camping difficult

I do not see the two "competing" per se as one is a free game and one is $40. Fundamentally there are some differences (tf2 isnt very team focused compared to overwatch). As for myself, there is no class in overwatch as rewarding to me as the Spy in TF2. Something about backstabbing and disguising gives me a huge thrill. Also, TF2 is more physics based (i.e. rocket jumps) and has less hitscan weapons than overwatch. To me, tf2 has a higher skillcap because of this. Overwatch is pretty easy to learn, sure there's lots of fun strategies to do but nothing that really requires dedicated practice other than landing headshots and being accurate (which is the same in any fps game).

Let me know what you other TF2 players think.
